issue.title: Fix zstd decomporession

repository.name: mitmproxy
repository.description: An interactive TLS-capable intercepting HTTP proxy for penetration testers and software developers.

issue.body:
#### Description

This is a fix to issue #6914 .

#### Checklist

 - [x] I have updated tests where applicable.
 - [x] I have added an entry to the CHANGELOG.

body:
@mhils raised a PR, also added test which would fail without the current fix (it wouldn't decompress the second frame, while the current fix it does).

For the reference, I'll include here a standalone python test to check this type of errors as well:
```python
#!/usr/bin/env python

import zstandard
import pyzstd
import io

# Create 1024b payload
test_content = 'a' * 1024

# Compress it
test_compressed = zstandard.compress(test_content.encode())  # 1 frame zstd

# Concat compressed frame, it'll result two frames, total size of 2048b payload
two_frames_zstd = test_compressed + test_compressed          # 2 frames zstd

# Save 2 frames payload to verify with zstd binary later
with open('test.zst', 'wb') as f:

    f.write(two_frames_zstd)


# Now, we're going uncompress the 2 frames payload using 3 different methods
dctx = zstandard.ZstdDecompressor()

print('zstandard.decomporess():')
print(len(zstandard.decompress(two_frames_zstd)))

print('pyzstd.decomporess():')
print(len(pyzstd.decompress(two_frames_zstd)))

print('zstandard.ZstdDecompressor().stream_reader()')
print(len(dctx.stream_reader(io.BytesIO(two_frames_zstd)).read()))
```

Currently, this will result the following:
```
zstandard.decomporess():
1024
pyzstd.decomporess():
2048
zstandard.ZstdDecompressor().stream_reader()
2048
```
Showing that zstandard.decomporess() only decompresses the first frame, while the two other alternatives the full payload. (I wrote the unit test based on this) This PR includes the 2nd option as you requested, using zstandard and stream_reader().

Also, running `zstd -l test.zst` will confirm that our compressed payload has two frames and the total uncompressed size of 2048b:
```bash
$ zstd -l test.zst 
Frames  Skips  Compressed  Uncompressed  Ratio  Check  Filename
     2      0     0.04 KB       2.00 KB  53.895   None  test.zst
```
Also, just a fun fact and my observation: AWS/CloudFront switched to zstd about two years ago, and based on my observation they split any payload into 64k chunks (which is equivalent to one frame), so if the payload is larger than 64k, you'll get only the first 64k without this fix in [content](https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/api/mitmproxy/http.html#Message.content) which will also break content.[json()](https://docs.mitmproxy.org/stable/api/mitmproxy/http.html#Message.json) if the payload happens to be application/json. With this fix, you'll get it all.

sendai

issue.title: Large zstd packets (those using multiple frames) fail to decompress

repository.name: kafka-python-ng
repository.description: Fork for Python client for Apache Kafka

issue.body:
The symptom:

.../site-packages/kafka/codec.py", line 315, in zstd_decode
    return zstd.ZstdDecompressor().decompress(payload)
           ^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^^
zstd.ZstdError: could not determine content size in frame header

This issue is discussed here: https://github.com/mitmproxy/mitmproxy/issues/6914

A fix inspired by that discussion that works for me:

--- a/kafka/codec.py
+++ b/kafka/codec.py
@@ -311,7 +311,4 @@ def zstd_encode(payload):
 def zstd_decode(payload):
     if not zstd:
         raise NotImplementedError("Zstd codec is not available")
-    try:
-        return zstd.ZstdDecompressor().decompress(payload)
-    except zstd.ZstdError:
-        return zstd.ZstdDecompressor().decompress(payload, max_output_size=ZSTD_MAX_OUTPUT_SIZE)
+    return zstd.ZstdDecompressor().stream_reader(io.BytesIO(payload)).read()
